solutions.check: 32 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Take off TV presenter and a rejected May

parts.note: Dec Donnelly, of the British TV double act Ant and Dec
taken as written

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Theresa May was Prime Minister, PM

explanation.surface: A television presenter and a spurned Theresa May both make a quick exit.
explanation.walkthrough: May is not the month but Theresa May, so she becomes PM, which is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, often secretly; taking off is the informal phrasal verb for that departure.

clue.text: Run an exposé: "ex-royal's mean!"

parts.note: Diana, the late Princess of Wales, former royal wife
the possessive ending taken as written
close can mean stingy, tight with money

explanation.surface: A tabloid splash quotes someone calling a former royal stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted headline reads as gossip; it actually supplies DI, S and CLOSE in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishing an exposé means revealing hidden facts, which is exactly to make them known or reveal them publicly.

clue.text: Links man said "It could protect one's member"

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked rings

indicators.note: said means spoken out loud, so we want a word that merely sounds right

parts.note: a man is a male, and male and mail sound identical

explanation.surface: A golfer from the links offers advice about protecting one's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Links suggests golf, but here it just means joined rings; member is a limb, with a cheeky second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour of interlocking metal rings guarded a knight's arms and legs, which are limbs, also called members.

clue.text: Dome's shambolic, ludicrous opening, a perfect example

indicators.note: something shambolic is in total disorder, so its letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written, with 's standing for 'is'

indicators.note: an opening is where a thing starts, so only its first letter counts

parts.note: the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sarcastic review of the Millennium Dome's chaotic, ridiculous launch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Millennium Dome's widely mocked opening night colours the surface; the anagram takes DOME plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is an ideal specimen or paragon worth copying, the standard others should follow.

clue.text: Carnal lay with chips scattered all over the place

indicators.note: things scattered everywhere end up in no fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tryst in which a bag of fried potatoes ends up strewn across the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lay and chips look like sex and food, but they are only the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal relates to bodily desires and the flesh, so a synonym is bodily, i.e. relating to the body.

clue.text: Fiery with press, Brand's producer

parts.note: fiery means burning
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Comedian Russell Brand's TV producer has a heated row with the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand looks like Russell Brand, the comedian, but it is the burn mark seared on to cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock are marked by searing their hide with heated metal, so this implement makes the mark.

clue.text: Sort of dress said to restrain a disciplinarian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gown with no shoulder straps
second meaning: the words one might use to tell a flogger to ease off with the belt

explanation.surface: A dress style somehow linked to calming down a strict schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second part as a spoken instruction: 'strap less', i.e. beat less with the strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gown held up without shoulder straps is a common style of evening wear.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) Given old money, former pop star becomes budding Saudi dictator?

parts.note: an old British coin worth five shillings
the late American singer of Purple Rain, known by a single royal-title name

explanation.surface: A dead pop singer handed old cash turns into a future Saudi strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: The crown was a pre-decimal British coin; Prince was the American pop star who died in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohammed bin Salman is heir to the Saudi throne, so the title marks a ruler-in-waiting.

clue.text: Parliamentary proposal: "Leader to be replaced by Left" — a cosmetic thing

indicators.note: the opening letter is swapped out for a different one

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a vote
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A Commons motion proposes swapping the party leader for someone from the Left, a mere cosmetic change.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader sounds political but simply means the first letter of the proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream or liquid applied to the skin is a typical beauty product, so it counts as a cosmetic.

clue.text: Dominatrix accessories all over new town

indicators.note: to be all over something is to surround it completely

parts.note: a dominatrix might wield canes
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A dominatrix's kit is strewn across a newly built town.
explanation.walkthrough: New town suggests a British planned town, but new is just N, wrapped by the canes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannes is a resort town on the French Riviera, famous for its film festival.

clue.text: Get erect quick and last out

parts.note: to get upright is to stand
fast means quick

explanation.surface: Smutty advice about rising rapidly and then lasting the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Get erect and last out invite a ribald reading; they are just standing and enduring.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to hold firm and keep going to the end without giving way, as steadfast soldiers do.

clue.text: A place to sleep or maybe love, by the way

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters are only one possible version, so they can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A spot for sleeping, or perhaps for lovemaking, at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a roadside romp; or is jumbled, then O and ST follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle at night on a perch where they sleep, and informally a person's bed is also called that.

clue.text: Ointment ingredient agitated loin to right of large one

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: an, like a, means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cream for an inflamed groin next to a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, to the right of means after, so the abbreviation and the article come first and the jumbled loin follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the grease from sheep's wool used as a base in creams and salves.

clue.text: Have a go at getting a beer in South American city

indicators.note: being in a place means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro in Brazil
beer is ordered by the pint

explanation.surface: Someone tries ordering a beer while visiting a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Have a go at looks like 'attempt', but it means attack or berate.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at someone is British idiom for criticising them fiercely, and to rip into is the same attack.

clue.text: Crown makes a superficial contribution to this victory token

definitions.text: Crown makes a superficial contribution to this
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the skin covering the top of the head, whose surface is the crown
second meaning: a trophy taken from a defeated enemy, or any prized win

explanation.surface: A royal crown adds a light touch to some trophy of triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown is the top of the head, not a royal one; superficial means on the surface, literally the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors once cut the head's skin from slain foes as trophies, so it now means any prize from a defeated rival.

clue.text: Chelsea type retirement income taken by Brenda?

parts.note: a pension is income paid in retirement
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the late Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen collecting a pension, like some Chelsea resident.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda', and ER is her royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea Pensioners are retired soldiers living at the Royal Hospital Chelsea in London, famous for scarlet coats.

clue.text: Some words that Archer was given

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a grammatical unit made of words
second meaning: the prison term handed to Jeffrey Archer for perjury

explanation.surface: A brief quote attributed to the novelist Jeffrey Archer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Tory peer, was jailed in 2001 for perjury.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's punishment is a sentence, and so is a grammatical string of words with a full stop.

clue.text: Old Europhobe wants location from which money can be extracted

definitions.text: from which money can be extracted
definitions.note: a relative clause, standing for the place from which money comes

parts.note: Sir Bill Cash, veteran Eurosceptic Tory MP
a point is a place or location

explanation.surface: An elderly Brexiteer seeks a spot where he can get his hands on money.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Cash was a long-serving Conservative MP and fierce opponent of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashpoint is the British term for an ATM, the street machine dispensing banknotes.

clue.text: (& 21dn.) Sad Trump lie: "OK, 'til I …" (sorry, it's that or nothing)

indicators.note: sad here means pitiful or in a sorry state, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A pitiful Trump fib trails off, followed by a curt take-it-or-leave-it apology.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and ellipsis make it look like a quote; the fodder is all the letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone they must accept a situation because no alternative will be offered.

clue.text: Cold, emotionless Clinton, not backing out, takes one state

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start
out means removed, so these letters are dropped from the name

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
CAL is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: An unfeeling Clinton, refusing to retreat, carries one state in the election.
explanation.walkthrough: Not reads backwards as TON, which is then removed from the end of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinical describes a detached, coolly efficient manner devoid of warmth or feeling.

clue.text: Parisian's frightfully nice, squashing up pimple?

definitions.note: an example: a citizen of Paris

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read from the bottom, backwards
to squash something is to press it tightly within, so one piece is squeezed inside
frightfully suggests something done in a terrible way, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written
a zit is slang for a spot or pimple

explanation.surface: A terribly polite Frenchman squeezes a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice could be the French city, a natural partner for Parisian, but here it is only letters to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parisian is a resident or national of the French capital, a citoyen in revolutionary terms.

clue.text: see 18dn.
"Dish" repulsed American number two? Not quite

indicators.note: something repulsed is driven back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: US is short for the United States

indicators.note: not quite means slightly short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a child's euphemism for excrement

explanation.surface: A disgusted American calls the dish almost excrement.
explanation.walkthrough: Number two looks like a deputy or second-in-command, but it is the toilet euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese food of vinegared rice with raw fish, served as a plated course.

clue.text: see 7dn.
Bolt with electric current inserted in balls — go berserk

parts.note: to bolt is to run off

indicators.note: inserted means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: balls is British slang for nonsense, as is rot
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Electrocuted in a painful place, someone bolts and goes wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls here means rubbish talk, not testicles; I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: To run riot is to behave wildly and without restraint, the same as losing control in a frenzy.

clue.text: Star turned up embracing former Bond

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms around, so one piece surrounds another
in a down answer, turning upwards reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the sun is a star
ex means former

explanation.surface: A celebrity shows up hugging an ex-James Bond actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Former Bond looks like Roger Moore or Sean Connery; former alone gives EX and Bond is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connection or link joining things together, and so is a bond.

clue.text: Cyclops article that is about Trump's extremes — for individual consumption?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the food rather than a noun

parts.note: the setter, Cyclops, refers to himself
the indefinite article

indicators.note: the extremes of something are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: The Cyclops columnist writes a piece about Trump's excesses, meant for private reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the setter's pseudonym, so it means 'me'; about is only a link, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie with a meat filling is typically baked in a single serving, eaten by one person alone.

clue.text: Mad King George getting in no matter what

indicators.note: to get in is to enter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: any as in 'any which way'
GR is the cipher of King George, Georgius Rex

explanation.surface: Mad King George III insists on getting his way regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: Mad King George evokes George III's madness, but mad is the definition, meaning cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in informal and American usage means furious or cross, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Nothing working for the President?

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A dig that nothing is working for the current President.
explanation.walkthrough: The President suggests whoever is in office now; the question mark warns it is a past one.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the 37th US President, who resigned over the Watergate scandal.

clue.text: Distort size (get it?) — that's the spirit

indicators.note: to distort is to twist out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Exaggerating one's size, with a nudge-nudge aside, is cheerfully encouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'get it?' reads as an aside about a double entendre; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeitgeist is German for 'time spirit', the prevailing mood or outlook of an era.

clue.text: 'Treasure' screwed her nine times, finally

indicators.note: screwed means twisted round, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lothario boasts of bedding his 'treasure' nine times.
explanation.walkthrough: Treasure is in quotation marks as a pet name, but it is the verb meaning to cherish.
explanation.definitionFit: To enshrine something is to cherish it as sacred, the verb sense of treasure.

clue.text: One yanked out of bed is an aphrodisiac?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shellfish harvested from the seabed where it grows
second meaning: a food reputed to stir sexual desire

explanation.surface: Someone dragged from bed proves to be quite the turn-on.
explanation.walkthrough: Bed suggests sleeping, but shellfish grow in beds on the sea floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellfish of this kind have long been reputed, with little evidence, to boost libido.
